subject: Post-demo: NimbleCart inference integration + routing next steps
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Dana Li <dana.li@nimblecart.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 25 Apr 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: NimbleCart inference integration + routing next steps

Hi Dana — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap + proposed next steps from our side so we keep momentum: 

Summary of what you highlighted: 
- Primary workload: product search + recommendations served via inline web requests (95% low-latency).
- Secondary workload: nightly embedding refresh + reranker for merchandising (batch).
- SLOs: 40–60ms p95 on search, budget target $0.20 / 1k tokens equivalent for inference.

Action items we discussed (owner / ETA):
1) SDK & auth kickoff: Tessa will send an SDK quickstart and sample auth configs (API key vs mTLS) — Tessa / 2026-04-28
2) Routing & fallbacks: propose latency-first routing in us-east with cost-fallback to a quantized variant and region-failover to us-west — Markus / 2026-04-29
3) Structured output/tool calling: we will prototype a constrained JSON schema for the search response + optional tool call for price checks — Tessa / 2026-05-05
4) Embeddings/re-ranker plan: batch embedding pipeline details + storage options (we recommended Redis for vector cache) — Markus / 2026-05-06

Attachments: I’ve attached the minimal mapping CSV and a mutual action plan with milestones.

Questions for you before Tessa kicks off:
- Do you want Redwood-managed keys (hosted) or do you prefer customer-managed TLS certs/KMS?
- Any hard region constraints (HIPAA/PHI concerns) for production?

If that looks right I’ll open a short tech thread and loop in engineering for a short architecture session next week.

Thanks,
Markus
Regional Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: nimblecart-mvp-mapping.csv (csv, 12KB), nimblecart-mutual-action-plan.pdf (pdf, 210KB)

From: Dana Li <dana.li@nimblecart.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@nimblecart.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Apr 2026 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: NimbleCart inference integration + routing next steps

Hi Markus — really helpful recap, thanks. Quick answers: 

- Auth: we prefer customer-managed keys (KMS) for production; for PoC, API keys are fine.
- Regions: primary production in us-east; we cannot send PHI to eu/apac. us-west is OK as a DR/failover zone.
- Cost target: $0.20 / 1k is our guideline but we can accept short-term tradeoffs for latency in search.

A couple of clarifications: 
- For reranking: we currently store candidate vectors in-house (Postgres + Faiss). We’re evaluating an external vector cache to reduce query latency.
- For structured output: we need strict schema validation on the JSON returned from the model — if the model calls an external price-check tool we must see a signed tool response token (for audit).

We’re available for a technical session Wednesday (2026-04-29) between 10–12 PT. Carlos will join the architecture call.

Best,
Dana
Head of Engineering
NimbleCart

--
Dana Li
NimbleCart | dana.li@nimblecart.com

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Dana Li <dana.li@nimblecart.com>, Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@nimblecart.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Apr 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: NimbleCart inference integration + routing next steps — SDK & auth details

Hi Dana / Carlos — quick tech follow-up ahead of today’s call. I attached a 5-minute SDK walkthrough and included a short checklist below to keep the call focused.

SDK & auth options (summary):
- PoC: Redwood SDK with API key (simple, no infra changes).
- Production: Customer-managed KMS + mutual TLS between your VPC and the Redwood Private gateway (recommended given you want control over keys). We can support both; we’ll provide sample Terraform snippets.

Routing & policy suggestions (initial proposal):
- Route policy name: nimblecart-search-latency-first
  - Primary: hosted model x-large (unquantized) in us-east, latency SLA p95=50ms
  - Fallback-1: quantized variant of same model in us-east (lower cost, slightly higher latency)
  - Fallback-2: region failover to us-west if us-east unavailable or >200ms
  - Cost guardrail: if 7-day rolling cost per request > $0.28 (above your target), automatically prefer quantized variant for new sessions

Structured output / tool calling:
- We’ll enforce Constrained JSON schema validation on responses. If a tool call (e.g., price-check) is emitted, the runtime will attach a signed tool token (HMAC) and we can log the tool response for audit.

Embeddings + reranker plan (short):
- Batch job nightly to compute embeddings; store canonical vectors in your S3 and optionally index in Faiss/Redis for low-latency lookups.
- For online reranking: Redis vector cache in us-east for 1–10ms vector lookups; call Redwood reranker with top-50 candidates.

Pre-call checklist (what I’ll demo):
- SDK install + auth sample (code snippet)
- Demo of routing policy switch (quantized vs unquantized)
- Example JSON schema enforcement and logged tool token

Scheduling: we’ll take the 10:30–11:15 PT slot if that still works. I’ll share a short architecture slide and code snippet to the Drive link in the MLP.

Thanks — Tessa
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-sdk-quickstart.md (md, 8KB)

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Apr 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: NimbleCart: internal follow-up — pricing guardrail & next internal steps

Sergio — summary from the tech call with NimbleCart (they’re aligned with our latency-first approach but want KMS for prod). Key asks and my recommendations: 

1) Routing policy & price guardrail: implement the "nimblecart-search-latency-first" policy Tessa proposed. Add an override window: allow 72-hr manual override to prefer unquantized for launch events, but enforce daily cost alerting and auto-fallback if running > $0.28/req.

2) Quantized variant pricing: please confirm unit price delta for the proposed quantized variant (we need to show cost math in the MAP).

3) KMS onboarding: Ops will need the onboarding checklist for customer-managed KMS + mTLS (Tessa, can you paste the Terraform snippet and cert rotation notes in the Drive folder?).

4) Next steps / timeline: PoC (API key) this week, Prod auth + routing policy sign-off next week, embedding/re-ranker pilot 2 weeks after that.

Can you take point on pricing delta and confirm by EOD tomorrow so I can update the MAP and the HubSpot deal?

Thanks,
Markus
Regional Sales, Redwood Inference
